subject: math
title: Partition Shapes into Equal Parts
seo_title: Grade 3 Partitioning Shapes Worksheets: Equal Parts, Unit Fractions and Area of Each Part
standard_text: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole. For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as 1/4 of the area of the shape.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 partitioning shapes worksheets with pictures: tell equal from unequal parts, name halves, thirds, fourths, sixths and eighths, see that equal parts can have different shapes, and find the area of each part on a grid. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Equal parts have the same area. Each part is 1 over the number of equal parts.
key_sub: Cut into 4 equal parts, each part is 1/4 of the whole. Equal parts can have different shapes: a triangle and a strip can both be 1/4 of the same square.
body_html:
Equal parts

To partition a shape means to cut it into parts. For fractions, the parts must be equal: they must have the same area (cover the same amount of space).

Name each part with a unit fraction

If a shape is cut into equal parts, each part is a unit fraction of the whole: 1 on top, the number of equal parts on the bottom.

Equal partsNameEach part
2halves12 (one half)
3thirds13 (one third)
4fourths14 (one fourth)
6sixths16 (one sixth)
8eighths18 (one eighth)

Same area, different shape

Equal parts do not have to be the same shape. They only need the same area.

On a grid, count the unit squares in each part to check.

Example

A rectangle has an area of 20 square units. It is split into 4 equal parts. What is the area of each part, and what fraction of the whole is it?

Equal parts share the area: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. There are 4 equal parts, so each is 14.

Answer: 5 square units, 14

Example

Mia and 2 friends share a sandwich equally. What fraction does each person get?

Mia and 2 friends are 3 people, so the sandwich is cut into 3 equal parts.

Answer: 13

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the parts without checking they are equalFirst check that every part has the same area
Thinking parts of different shapes cannot be equalCompare the area, not the shape. Count squares on a grid
Calling 1 shaded part out of 4 “13” (1 shaded, 3 white)The bottom number is all the parts: 14
Counting the cut lines instead of the partsCount the parts: 3 cut lines can make 4 parts
Using the squares in one part as the bottom numberThe bottom number is the number of equal parts

faq.q: What does partition shapes mean in 3rd grade math?
faq.a: It means cutting a shape into parts with equal area, then naming each part with a unit fraction. A rectangle cut into 4 equal parts has parts that are each 1/4 of its area.

faq.q: Do equal parts have to be the same shape?
faq.a: No. Equal parts need the same area, not the same shape. A square cut on both diagonals and a square cut into 4 strips both have parts that are 1/4 of the square.

faq.q: How do you find the area of each equal part?
faq.a: Divide the area of the whole by the number of equal parts. A rectangle of 12 square units cut into 4 equal parts has parts of 3 square units, and each part is 1/4 of the whole.
A unit fraction has 1 on top, like 1/2, 1/3 or 1/8. It names one of the equal parts that make the whole.

items.e: 24 ÷ 6 = 4, so there are 4 equal beds. One bed is 14 of the garden. The bottom number is the number of beds, not the size of a bed.

items.q: Kai folds a sheet of paper in half, then in half again the same way. He opens it and sees 4 equal strips. Each strip is what fraction of the paper?

items.q: Ruby and 2 friends share a chocolate bar of 12 equal squares. Each person gets the same amount. How much does each person get?
items.e: Ruby and 2 friends are 3 people. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 squares each, and each share is 13 of the bar.

items.q: A square garden is split into 4 equal parts. Ava plants beans in 1 part. What fraction of the garden has no beans?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts. 1 part has beans, so 3 parts have no beans: 34.

items.q: Omar splits a rectangle of 4 by 2 unit squares into 2 equal parts shaped like stairs. What is the area of each part?
items.e: The rectangle has 4 × 2 = 8 unit squares. 2 equal parts: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 square units each. The stair shape does not change the area.

items.q: Jack wants to split a rectangle of 6 by 2 unit squares into 3 equal parts. How many unit squares should each part have?
items.e: The rectangle has 6 × 2 = 12 squares. 3 equal parts: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 squares in each part, and each part is 13 of the rectangle.
